summary: Côte d'Ivoire's NDC ecosystem pledges span restoration, conservation, and agriculture, with major quantitative targets. Restoration commitments include restoring up to 4 million hectares through conservation, reforestation, and agroforestry, restoring 20% of forest cover by 2030, and reforesting 1.5 million hectares by 2035, alongside converting 3 million hectares of land to forest by 2030. Conservation targets aim to place 80% of national forest area under sustainable management by 2035, protect 30% of terrestrial and marine ecosystems, limit forest cover loss to 550,000 hectares by 2035, and expand the protected-area network. Agriculture pledges focus on transforming 2.5 million hectares of cropland into agroforestry systems and scaling climate-smart practices to 80% of vulnerable farming operations. Cross-cutting commitments include eliminating deforestation in agricultural value chains, developing 10 million hectares of jurisdictional REDD+ programs, and engaging 200,000 women and youth in sustainable natural resource management, with the forestry sector targeted as a carbon sink (−150% emissions) by 2030.
